For I am jealous--</hi>The justification of his self-commendations lies in his zealous care lest they should fall from Christ, to whom he, as "the friend of the Bridegroom" (<reference osisRef="John.3.29">Joh 3:29</reference>), has espoused them; in order to lead them back from the false apostles to Christ, he is obliged to boast as an apostle of Christ, in a way which, but for the motive, would be "folly."<div eID="gen34644" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34645" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">godly jealousy--</hi>literally, "jealousy of God" (compare <reference osisRef="2Cor.1.12">2Co 1:12</reference>, "godly sincerity," literally, "sincerity of God"). "If I am immoderate, I am immoderate to God" [Bengel]. A jealousy which has God's honor at heart (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.19.10">1Ki 19:10</reference>).<div eID="gen34645" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34646" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I ... espoused you--</hi>Paul uses a Greek term applied properly to the bridegroom, just as he ascribes to himself "jealousy," a feeling properly belonging to the husband; so entirely does he identify himself with Christ.<div eID="gen34646" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34647" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">present you as a chaste virgin to Christ--</hi>at His coming, when the heavenly marriage shall take place (<reference osisRef="Matt.25.6">Mt 25:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.19.7">Re 19:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.19.9">9</reference>). What Paul here says he desires to do, namely, "present" the Church as "a chaste virgin" to Christ, Christ Himself is said to do in the fuller sense. Whatever ministers do effectively, is really done by Christ (<reference osisRef="Eph.5.27-Eph.5.32">Ep 5:27-32</reference>). The espousals are going on now. He does not say "chaste virgins"; for not individual members, but the whole body of believers conjointly constitute the Bride. <div eID="gen34647" type="x-p"/>

But at this time, A.D. 38 or 39, three years after Paul's conversion, A.D. 36, Aretas, against whom the Emperor Tiberius as the ally of Herod Agrippa had sent an army under Vitellius, had got possession of Damascus on the death of the emperor, and the consequent interruption of Vitellius' operations.
